qs.q: A patient is given a drug that blocks nicotinic receptors at the neuromuscular junction. What is the immediate physiological consequence on end-plate potentials?
o: Hyperpolarization that prevents reaching the threshold potential.
Immediate enzymatic degradation of neurotransmitter vesicles at the synapse.
Sustained depolarization that inactivates voltage‑gated channels.
Enhanced acetylcholine release attempting to compensate for receptor loss.
Failure to reach threshold because end‑plate potentials are absent.
qs.e: Blocking postsynaptic nicotinic receptors prevents acetylcholine from generating a sufficient end-plate potential to reach muscle threshold.
